title.rendered: watchOS 26 Supports These Apple Watch Models

content.rendered:
Apple finally took the wraps off the next-gen operating system for the Apple Watch. As expected, the version is called watchOS 26 instead of watchOS 12. The new OS features advanced health monitoring capabilities, AI-powered insights, and enhanced fitness tools. But the big question remains: Does your Apple Watch support watchOS 26? We’ve got you covered.

Breaking the usual pattern, watchOS 26 continues to support the Apple Watch Series 6, which was introduced in 2020. This marks the sixth major software update for the device—extending its support beyond the expected timeline

Apple Watch Models That Support watchOS 26 (Complete List)

Here’s a list of all Apple Watch models that support watchOS 26 as per Apple:

  • Apple Watch Ultra (1st and 2nd generation)
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Series 8
  • Apple Watch Series 7
  • Apple Watch Series 6
  • Apple Watch SE (2nd generation)

Additionally, the Apple Watch Series 11 and Apple Watch Ultra 3, launching in September 2025, will ship with watchOS 26 pre-installed.

Apple Watch Models that Won’t Support watchOS 26

Apple typically provides five years of watchOS updates for its wearables. In 2024, with the release of watchOS 11, the company dropped support for the Apple Watch Series 4 and Series 5.

watchOS 26 release timeline: Developer beta, Public beta & stable rollout

Here’s when you can expect to try watchOS 26:

  • June 9, 2025: Apple has already seeded the watchOS 26 developer beta immediately after the WWDC keynote.
  • July 2025: The public beta of watchOS 26 will be available. (Note: You’ll need the iOS 26 beta installed on your iPhone to install the watchOS 26 beta.)
  • September–October 2025: The stable watchOS 26 release will roll out to all compatible devices alongside the official launch of iOS 19.

Signing off…

If you own an Apple Watch Series 6 or newer, you’re in the clear and will get to enjoy everything watchOS 26 has to offer. Otherwise, it might be time to consider an upgrade to take advantage of all the new features coming in 2025.

Did your Apple Watch make the cut? Drop a comment below and let us know!

title.rendered: Why Is My iPhone So Slow? How to Make an iPhone Faster

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Reasons Why Your iPhone Is Slow: Full storage, battery wear, outdated iOS, and background tasks often slow down performance or cause lag.
  • Restart and Free Up Storage: Rebooting your iPhone and deleting unused apps or media quickly frees up memory and clears system glitches.
  • Keep iOS and Apps Updated: Installing the latest iOS and app versions ensures your iPhone runs with the newest fixes, security patches, and optimizations.
  • Monitor Battery Health and Manage Power: A worn-out battery can throttle speed; check Battery Health and avoid Low Power Mode unless necessary.
  • Optimize Settings and Habits for Longevity: Turn off motion effects, minimize widgets, and clean up regularly to keep your iPhone running fast longer.

Your iPhone wasn’t always like this. Once, it opened apps in a snap, ran smoothly, and never froze mid-scroll. Now? It lags, stutters, and even typing feels like a chore. You’re not alone – iPhones can slow down over time. But that doesn’t mean it’s old or broken.

In this guide, we’ll explain why your iPhone is running slow and how to fix it—from simple setting tweaks to deep cleanups that’ll make it feel brand new again. Let’s speed things up.

Why Is My iPhone So Slow?

Before you jump into fixes, it’s essential to understand what might be causing the slowdown.

  1. Full Storage: When your iPhone is nearly full, it doesn’t have enough space for temporary files, app caches, and background processes. This leads to lagging, camera delays, and choppy typing.
  2. Battery Health Decline: A degraded battery can’t supply enough power to the processor, prompting iOS to throttle performance to prevent unexpected shutdowns.
  3. Too Many Background Processes: Multiple apps running in the background, constant widget updates, and location services consume memory—slowing down the tasks that matter to you.
  4. Outdated Software or Apps: Older iOS versions or apps can become buggy and inefficient. Updates usually fix performance glitches and improve speed.
  5. Low Power Mode: While Low Power Mode saves battery, it reduces animations and limits background activity, making your iPhone feel sluggish.
  6. Extreme Temperatures: Using your iPhone in extreme heat or cold forces the system to slow down to protect internal components.
  7. Performance Management Is On: iOS may automatically enable performance management after unexpected shutdowns, reducing speed to ensure stability.
  8. Malware or Unofficial Apps: Rare, but possible—especially on jailbroken devices. Malware or sketchy apps can hog system resources in the background.
  9. Poor Network Conditions: A weak Wi-Fi or cellular signal can make apps feel unresponsive. It’s often mistaken for overall slowness.
  10. Recent iOS Update: Your iPhone may feel sluggish post-update due to indexing and background optimization. A restart usually fixes it.

How to Make Your iPhone Faster

Now that you know what causes the lag, let’s fix it.

1. Restart Your iPhone

A simple restart clears system memory and resolves temporary bugs.

  1. Press and hold the power and volume button.
  2. Drag the slider to turn off.
  3. Wait 30 seconds, then turn it back on.

2. Free Up Storage

iPhones need free space to work efficiently. Try to keep at least 10–15% storage free.

  1. Go to Settings > General > iPhone Storage.

  2. Wait a moment while your iPhone analyzes storage usage.
  3. You’ll see a list of apps, along with the amount of space each is using.
  4. Tap any app to either Offload App (remove the app but keep its data) or Delete App (remove both app and data).

  5. Choose to offload or delete apps you rarely use or that take up too much space.

Once you’ve cleared unused apps and media, the next step is to clean up other types of data that can silently fill your storage and slow things down. These include cached browsing files and old message history.

  1. For browsing data, go to Settings > Apps > Safari and tap Clear History and Website Data to clean up old web files. You can do the same for any other browser you use. 

  2. If you’re running low on space, consider setting messages to auto-delete. Go to Settings > Apps > Messages > Keep Messages and set it to auto-delete messages older than 30 Days or 1 Year. 

3. Update iOS and Apps

Updating your iPhone and its apps can help resolve bugs that may be slowing down your device. New iOS versions often iron out small glitches that you might not even notice but can still affect performance.

  1. Go to Settings > General > Software Update.

  2. Tap Download and Install if available.

For Apps:

  • Open the App Store, tap your profile, and choose Update All.

4. Check Battery Health

A degraded battery can slow your iPhone down because it can no longer provide enough power during heavy tasks. When this happens, iOS reduces performance to avoid unexpected shutdowns.

To check your battery health:

  1. Go to Settings > Battery.
  2. Tap Battery Health.
  3. Check the Maximum Capacity percentage. If it’s below 80%, it may be time for a battery replacement.

You can get it replaced at an Apple Store or an authorized service center for the best results.

5. Turn Off Low Power Mode

Low Power Mode saves battery by reducing the amount of work your iPhone has to do. It reduces animations, limits background tasks, and slows down the processor. That’s why your phone may feel sluggish when it’s on. If you want better speed and performance, it’s better to turn it off when you don’t need to save battery.

  1. Go to Settings > Battery.
  2. Turn off Low Power Mode.

6. Disable Background App Refresh

Disabling this setting prevents apps from using system resources in the background. It frees up memory and processor power, which helps your iPhone run smoother, especially if you have many apps installed.

  1. Go to Settings > General > Background App Refresh.
  2. Turn it off completely or disable it for specific apps.

7. Remove Widgets and Reduce Motion

Widgets and animations consume memory and graphics resources. Removing them can help your iPhone respond faster, especially on older models.

  • Long-press a widget and select Remove Widget.

To reduce motion:

  1. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Motion.
  2. Turn on Reduce Motion.

However, removing animations can make your iPhone feel less fluid, which may affect the user experience.

8. Reset All Settings (Optional)

Resetting all settings can fix hidden issues that may be causing your iPhone to lag. It doesn’t erase your data but restores all settings to default, which can help clear out software conflicts.

  1. Go to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone.

  2. Tap Reset > Reset All Settings.

9. Factory Reset (Last Resort)

A factory reset wipes your iPhone completely and reinstalls the system, which can eliminate deep issues that nothing else fixes. Use this only as a last resort, and be sure to back up your data beforehand.

  1. Go to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone.
  2. Tap Erase All Content and Settings.

  3. Follow the prompts to complete the reset.

How to Keep Your iPhone Fast Over Time

Making your iPhone faster once is great, but keeping it fast is even better. These small habits can help your device stay smooth in the long run.

  1. Set regular cleanup reminders: Set monthly cleanup reminders to remove unused apps, clear Safari data, and manage your storage. Regular cleanups prevent your iPhone from becoming cluttered with unnecessary files that can slow it down.
  2. Restart weekly: A quick restart once a week clears temporary files and small glitches. This helps your phone stay smooth and responsive.
  3. Limit widget use: Only keep widgets you actually use. Too many widgets constantly update in the background and can slow things down over time.
  4. Keep apps updated: Make sure your apps are always on the latest version. App updates often fix slowdowns and improve speed.
  5. Avoid overheating: Don’t use your iPhone in direct sunlight or while charging for long hours. Heat can slow down performance over time.
  6. Turn off features you don’t use: Features like AirDrop, Bluetooth, and location services drain resources. Turning them off when not needed helps free up power for what you are actively doing.

Also Read: Best iPhone Cleaner Apps to Maximize Your Storage

When It’s Time for a New iPhone

If your battery is dying, storage is always full, and performance hasn’t improved even after resets, it might be time for an upgrade. Especially if your current device no longer supports iOS updates.

Pro Tip: Check Apple’s trade-in program—you might get a sweet discount on your next iPhone.

Video: 6 Awesome Tips to Boost iPhone Speed

Final Words – The Simple Fix for a Slow iPhone

iPhones slow down for reasons—like storage bloat, battery issues, or outdated software. The good news? Most problems are fixable. Start with a restart, clear the clutter, turn off unnecessary features, and keep your device up to date. These simple steps can breathe new life into your iPhone—no Genius Bar appointment required.

  • Apple Watch Too Slow? Tips to Speed Up Your Apple Watch
  • How to Fast Charge iPhone and iPad (Ultimate Guide)
  • How to Speed Up a Slow Mac

keyPoints.title: Reasons Why Your iPhone Is Slow
keyPoints.explanation: Various factors like full storage, degraded battery, background processes, outdated software, and extreme temperatures can cause your iPhone to lag or run slowly.

keyPoints.title: Restart and Free Up Storage
keyPoints.explanation: A simple restart clears temporary bugs, and freeing storage by deleting unused apps and clearing cache can significantly improve performance.

keyPoints.title: Keep iOS and Apps Updated
keyPoints.explanation: Updating to the latest iOS version and apps fixes bugs and glitches that may be slowing down your device.

keyPoints.title: Monitor Battery Health and Manage Power
keyPoints.explanation: Degraded batteries can throttle performance; replacing the battery and turning off Low Power Mode when not needed can help maintain speed.

keyPoints.title: Optimize Settings and Habits for Longevity
keyPoints.explanation: Disabling unnecessary features like widgets, reducing motion, and regular cleaning, along with optional resets, can keep your iPhone running smoothly over time.

title.rendered: Keep It Private: How to Hide Photos and Videos on iPhone, iPad, and Mac

content.rendered:
Your iPhone, iPad, and Mac often hold more than just pictures—they’re home to your most personal memories. Whether it’s sensitive documents, private moments, or personal videos, Apple gives you built-in tools to protect them.

In this detailed guide, I’ll show you how to hide and unhide photos and videos on your iPhone, iPad, and Mac—plus tips to keep them private and secure.

Why Hide Photos or Videos on Your iPhone, iPad, or Mac?

Your devices are packed with memories—some you don’t want others to stumble upon. Here’s why you may want to hide specific content:

  • Keep personal moments and documents away from others’ eyes.
  • Avoid accidental exposure when handing your device to someone.
  • Remove clutter from your main gallery.
  • Prevent sensitive content like IDs or bank information from being visible.

Apple’s Hidden album lets you store this content safely—and lock it with Face ID, Touch ID, or a passcode.

How to Hide Photos and Videos on iPhone or iPad

Hiding pictures and videos on your iPhone or iPad is easy with the built-in Photos app. 

Hide a Single Image or Video:

  1. Open the Photos app and select the image or video you want to hide.
  2. Tap the More icon (three dots) in the top-right corner.
  3. Select Hide, then confirm.

Hide Multiple Images or Videos:

  1. Open Photos, then tap Select.
  2. Select all the images or videos you want to hide.
  3. Tap the More icon at the bottom-right corner.
  4. Select Hide, and confirm.

     

Access the Hidden Album:

The Hidden album is where all your hidden photos and videos are stored. To access and manage it: 

  1. Open the Photos app. 
  2. Scroll to Utilities, then tap Hidden.
  3. Tap View Album and authenticate with Face ID, Touch ID, or your passcode if the album is locked. 

  4. View or delete a photo from your Hidden items:
    • To view a photo or video, tap it to open. 
    • To delete an item, select it, tap the Trash icon, and confirm.

       

To Unhide a Photo or Video: 

  1. Go to the Hidden album, tap Select.
  2. Select the photo or video to unhide.
  3. Tap the More icon and select Unhide.

      

It will reappear in your main Photos library.

How to Hide Photos and Videos on Mac

Hiding photos or videos on a Mac is just as easy using the Photos app.

Hide a Single Item:

  1. Launch the Photos app on your Mac. 
  2. Find the photo or video you want to hide and double-click to open it. 
  3. Control-click the image or video, or click the Image menu at the top. 
  4. Select Hide 1 Photo or Hide 1 Video and click Hide. 

The item will move to the Hidden album. 

Hide Multiple Photos and Videos: 

  1. Open the Photos app. 
  2. Hold the Command (⌘) key and click each photo or video you want to hide. 
  3. Control-click any selected item or go to the Image menu. 
  4. Choose Hide [number] Photos/Videos and confirm your choice. 

The selected items will move to the Hidden album. 

Access the Hidden Album:

To view or manage your hidden photos on a Mac: 

  1. Go to the Photos app. 
  2. Click View in the menu bar and select Show Hidden Photo Album.

     
  3. The Hidden album will appear in the sidebar under Utilities. 
  4. Click View Album on the right and use your Touch ID or Mac password. 
  5. Now, you can view your hidden photos or videos. 

To Unhide a Photo or Video: 

  1. From the Photos app, navigate to the Hidden album. 
  2. Select the photo or video you want to unhide. 
  3. Control-click and choose Unhide 1 Photo, or go to the Image menu and select Unhide Photo. 

     

The item will return to your main library.

How to Lock and Hide the Hidden Album

Apple gives you the option to lock and even hide the Hidden album for extra security.

On iPhone or iPad:

  1. Go to Settings > Apps > Photos. 
  2. Ensure Use Face ID is turned on. 
  3. Toggle off the Show Hidden Album option to remove it from the Photos app view.

To access it again, you need to toggle on the option. It’s best when you lend your phone to someone, and they know your device’s passcode.

On Mac:

  • The Hidden album is protected by your system password or Touch ID.
  • You won’t see it in the sidebar unless you enable it from the View menu.

Important Tips to Keep Photos Truly Private

  • Hidden Album Visibility: It’s still accessible unless you toggle it off. Use with caution.
  • iCloud Sync: Hidden photos sync across devices but remain hidden.
  • Backups: They’re included in backups—so keep your backups secure.
  • Search: Hidden items don’t appear in the search unless accessed directly.
  • Not Encrypted by Default: For full encryption, use locked Notes or third-party apps.

Bonus Tips to Secure Your Private Content

  • Use Locked Notes: Move sensitive photos to a locked note in the Notes app.
  • Enable two-factor authentication for your Apple ID.
  • Use privacy apps like Private Photo Vault for encryption.
  • Review your Hidden album regularly and clean it up as needed.
  • Lock the Photos App itself using iOS 18’s new app lock features.

Troubleshooting: Hidden Album or Unhide Option Not Working?

If you’re having trouble: 

  1. Hidden Album Not Visible: 
    • On iPhone/iPad: Go to Settings > Photos and toggle on Show Hidden Album. 
    • On Mac: In the Photos app, go to View > Show Hidden Photo Album. 
  2. Can’t Access Hidden Album: Ensure you’re using the correct Face ID, Touch ID, or passcode. If you’re locked out, reset your device passcode via the Settings menu. 
  3. Unhide Option Missing: Make sure you’re in the Hidden album and have selected the photo or video. Try force-quitting the Photos app and then reopening it. 
  4. Sync issues: If hidden photos aren’t syncing across all your devices, ensure that iCloud Photos is turned on. To do this, go to Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > Photos.  

Protect Your Privacy with Hidden Albums! 

Hiding photos and videos on iPhone, iPad, and Mac is a simple yet powerful way to keep your private moments secure. Whether you’re concerned about accidental exposure or want to keep your personal media under wraps, Apple makes it easy.

It’s worth taking a few minutes to lock down your memories—you’ll thank yourself later.

FAQs

Can I hide photos in the Notes app instead?

Yes. Create a note, attach the photo, and lock the note using a password, Face ID, or Touch ID. The photo will no longer appear in the Photos app.

Is the Hidden Album encrypted?

Not entirely. While it’s protected by biometrics or passcode, it’s not encrypted. Use third-party apps for added protection.

Do hidden photos sync across devices?

Yes. They stay hidden on all devices if iCloud Photos is enabled. Use two-factor authentication to keep your account secure.

  • How to combine photos on your iPhone

title.rendered: How to Use FaceTime on iPhone, iPad, and Mac?

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Initial Setup: Set up FaceTime by signing in with your Apple ID and enabling it in your device’s settings.
  • Key Requirements: To use FaceTime, you need a compatible Apple device, a stable internet connection, and an Apple ID.
  • Making Calls: Start calls by selecting a contact in the FaceTime app; you can answer or decline incoming alerts.
  • Advanced Features: Enhance calls with screen sharing, Memoji, video reactions, and background blur for more interactive chats.
  • Troubleshooting: Fix common issues by checking your internet connection, updating your device, or verifying FaceTime settings.

FaceTime is Apple’s built-in video and audio calling app that lets you stay connected with friends, family, and colleagues across iPhone, iPad, and Mac. With recent updates, FaceTime now includes fun and practical features such as screen sharing, reactions, and the ability to invite non-Apple users.

In this guide, I’ll walk you through setting up and using FaceTime, exploring its best features, and troubleshooting common issues.

Table of Contents
  • How do I set up FaceTime on iPhone/iPad or Mac?
  • Prerequisites for Using FaceTime
  • How to Set Up FaceTime
    • On iPhone or iPad
    • On Mac
  • How to Make and Receive FaceTime Calls
    • Initiate a Call
    • Using FaceTime Links
    • Receiving Calls
    • Create Group FaceTime Calls
  • Explore FaceTime Features
    • 1. Capture Live Photos
    • 2. Use FaceTime Filters
    • 3. Add Texts, Stickers, and Shapes
    • 4. Use Memoji during FaceTime call
    • 5. Fun with Reactions and Gestures
    • 6. Blur Your Background During FaceTime Calls
    • 7. Video Effects (iPad & Mac)
    • 8. Share Screen with FaceTime
    • 9. Enable Eye Contact
    • 10. Record Video Message
    • 11. Delete Call Log
  • How to Schedule FaceTime Calls
  • Advanced FaceTime Tips
    • 1. Remove Background Noise
    • 2. Handoff Between Devices
    • 3. Use Live Captions
    • 4. Announce FaceTime calls
    • 5. Record FaceTime Calls with Audio
  • FaceTime Privacy & Safety Tips
  • Troubleshooting FaceTime Issues
  • Stay Connected with FaceTime!

How do I set up FaceTime on iPhone/iPad or Mac?

Prerequisites for Using FaceTime

Before using FaceTime, make sure you have:

  • An iPhone, iPad, or Mac running iOS 18, iPadOS 18, or macOS Sequoia. Older versions (like iOS 17) work but might miss some newer features.
  • An Apple ID. If you don’t have one, create it for free at appleid.apple.com.
  • A stable internet connection (Wi-Fi or cellular) for smooth calls.
  • Access to camera and microphone (enabled in Settings).
  • FaceTime must be available in your country (not available in UAE and some other regions).
Tip Video calls can use a lot of data, so monitor your usage if you’re on a cellular plan.

How to Set Up FaceTime

Setting up FaceTime is quick and straightforward. Here’s how to do it on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac. 

On iPhone or iPad

  1. Open the Settings app.
  2. Tap Apps and select FaceTime. 
  3. Toggle FaceTime ON.

  4. Sign in with your Apple ID.
  5. Under “You Can Be Reached By FaceTime At,” choose your email or number.

If FaceTime doesn’t activate, wait a few minutes or check your internet connection. You may need to sign out and back in. 

On Mac

  1. Launch the FaceTime app from Applications or via Spotlight.
  2. Sign in with your Apple ID.
  3. Click FaceTime in the menu bar → Settings.
  4. Choose your caller ID and ensure the internet connection is stable.

If you see the FaceTime Waiting for Activation error, ensure your internet connection is stable, and your Apple ID has been verified.

How to Make and Receive FaceTime Calls

Once FaceTime is set up, you can start making and receiving calls. Here’s how. 

Initiate a Call

  1. Open the FaceTime app on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac. 
  2. Tap or click New FaceTime. 
  3. Enter a contact’s name, phone number, or email linked to their Apple ID. Otherwise, select the “+” button to open your contact list and select one. 

  4. Tap the camera icon for video or the phone icon for audio. On Mac, click the camera icon for video call or click the down arrow next to it and select FaceTime Audio.

Quick Tips:

  • In Messages, tap the video icon on the top-right to start a call.
  • Use Hey Siri: “FaceTime [Contact Name]” for hands-free calls.
  • Use the Contacts app to start FaceTime directly.

Using FaceTime Links

FaceTime links allow you to invite anyone, including users of Android or Windows devices, to join a call via a web browser. Here’s how: 

  1. Open the FaceTime app and tap Create Link. 
  2. Share it via Messages, Mail, or third–party apps.

  3. Others can join through a web browser.

To allow someone to join the call, click the right tick next to their name. If you want to remove a participant from the call once they have joined, click the remove button (gray cross icon) within 30 seconds. 

Receiving Calls

  • When someone calls you, you’ll see the Answer or Decline buttons. To join the video call, tap the camera icon and tap Join. 
  • On iPhone/iPad, tap the call banner for more options, like sending a message or setting a reminder. 
  • FaceTime also features the ability to ‘Hold & Accept’ calls. If you are on a FaceTime call, and a call — regular or another FaceTime — comes up, you can use the ‘Hold & Accept’ option to put the call on waiting. 
  • On Mac, click Accept or Decline in the notification. If you want to answer in audio instead of video, click the down arrow next to Accept and select Audio. 
  • If you have multiple Apple devices, you can answer a call on any device signed into the same Apple ID. For example, answer an iPhone call on your Mac.

Create Group FaceTime Calls

FaceTime supports up to 32 participants in a Group FaceTime call.

To start:

  1. Open FaceTime and tap New FaceTime. 
  2. Add multiple contacts by typing their names, numbers, or emails. 
  3. Tap FaceTime to start a video call or the call icon for an audio call. 

  4. During the call, you can add more people from the info icon or sidebar. 

You can also start a group call from a Messages group chat by tapping the FaceTime icon at the top and selecting FaceTime Video. 

Explore FaceTime Features

FaceTime offers a range of fun and practical features to enhance your calls. Here’s a look at the best ones in iOS 18, iPadOS 18, and macOS Sequoia. 

1. Capture Live Photos 

You can snap a photo during a video call to capture a moment. 

  • Ensure Live Photos is enabled in Settings > Apps > FaceTime (iPhone/iPad) or FaceTime > Settings (Mac). Moreover, both participants must have Live Photos enabled. 
  • During a call, tap the shutter button (white circle) to take a photo. 

Your friend will now receive a notification about it. The Live Photos get saved to your Photos app.  

2. Use FaceTime Filters

FaceTime offers fun visual effects like comic book or sepia tones on iPhone and iPad. It applies in real-time and works on both front and rear cameras. 

  1. During a call, tap the screen, then tap the flower icon. 
  2. Select the Filters icon and choose a filter from the menu. 
  3. To remove the active filter, select the Original option and tap Close. 

3. Add Texts, Stickers, and Shapes 

Similar to Filters, you can add text labels, shapes, or stickers to your video feed. Perfect for playful calls or presentations.

  1. Tap the flower icon on your video feed during a call. 
    • To add a text label: Select the Aa icon. It will show different typefaces. Select one, enter your text, and place it in the desired place. 
    • For shapes: Tap the scribble icon and swipe up to get all available shapes. Tap any shape and adjust it. 
    • To add a sticker: Select the Stickers icon, tap a Sticker, and place it the way you like it. 

4. Use Memoji during FaceTime call 

If you are camera shy or want to have some fun, you can replace your face with an Animoji or custom Memoji character during a FaceTime call on iPhone and iPad. You can create your own Memoji avatar in the Messages app beforehand. 

  1. Tap the flower icon and select the Memoji option. 
  2. Pick any 3D avatar you like.

  3. Now, the receiver will hear everything you say, with Memoji doing the talking in real-time. 
  4. Select None from the Memoji feature to remove the avatar. 
  5. Tap Close to return to normal video call. 

5. Fun with Reactions and Gestures 

Sharing good news or wishing someone on FaceTime? You can fill their screen with 3D animated effects like hearts, confetti, or fireworks with FaceTime hand gestures.  

  1. During a call, open Control Center, select FaceTime Controls, and ensure Reactions option is enabled. For Mac, click the video icon in the menu and select Reactions. 
  2. Now, make hand gestures like a thumbs-up (for balloons) or peace sign (for confetti) and hold it for a few seconds to trigger the effect. Ensure your hands are away from your face. 
  3. Disable Reactions in the same way if they’re distracting. 

6. Blur Your Background During FaceTime Calls 

Blurring your background during video calls helps keep the focus on you and hides any distractions behind you. This feature is known as Portrait Mode in FaceTime. 

  1. Tap/click on your video tile to expand it. 
  2. Select the Portrait Mode (ƒ) icon on your tile.

     
  3. Your background will instantly blur, keeping you focused.  

To disable the blur effect, tap the Portrait Mode icon again.

You can also change the blurriness from Control Center > FaceTime Controls > Portrait and drag the Depth slider. On Mac, click the video icon on the menu bar, click the right arrow next to Portrait, and adjust the slider. 

Tip: On Mac, you can change your background and set a virtual image. Click the video icon on the menu bar, select Background, and choose a solid color or preset image. It also lets you use your own backdrop.

7. Video Effects (iPad & Mac)

FaceTime on iPad and Mac offers a suite of video effects that enhance your video calls, making them more engaging and expressive. 

  • Center Stage: It uses machine learning to keep you centered in the frame as you move. During a FaceTime call, click the video icon in the menu bar. Select Center Stage to enable or disable the feature. For iPad, go to Control Center > FaceTime Controls > Center Stage. 
  • Studio Light: This feature dims your background and illuminates your face for better visibility. Click the video icon in the menu bar and select Studio Light to toggle the effect. On iPad, go to Control Center > FaceTime Controls > Studio Light.

     
  • Presenter Overlay: It allows you to appear alongside your shared content. During a call, click the Share icon and select Share This Window. It will start screen sharing. Click the share icon in the menu bar, select Presenter Overlay, and choose between Small or Large. 

8. Share Screen with FaceTime

You can share your screen to show apps, photos, movies, or presentations thanks to the SharePlay integration. Moreover, it lets you play games over FaceTime calls. 

  1. During a call, tap the screen, then tap the Share icon. 
  2. Select Share My Screen. You can choose to share a specific screen on a Mac or iPad. 
  3. If you want to watch content or play a game, select the suitable app under Listen and Play Together (e.g., Apple TV, Disney+). 

9. Enable Eye Contact 

Generally, when video calling, we’re either looking at the person or ourselves during the call. So, due to this, our eyes appear to be looking downwards. 

FaceTime has a feature that ‘maintains eye contact’ during the call. In other words, the other person sees that you are looking at them instead of the screen, making your gaze more natural. 

  • On iPhone/iPad, enable it in Settings > Apps > FaceTime > Eye Contact. 
  • On Mac, it’s enabled by default on supported models. 

10. Record Video Message 

If someone doesn’t answer your call, you can leave a video message: 

  1. When the call goes to voicemail, tap Record Video. 
  2. The countdown will begin. Once recorded, tap the stop icon and hit Send.
  3. The recipient can view it in the FaceTime app. 

11. Delete Call Log 

If you frequently use FaceTime, your call history can be a mess. Clear it to save space: 

  • On iPhone or iPad: Open FaceTime, scroll down the call list and swipe left on a call to delete it. 

  • On Mac: Right-click a call and select Remove from Recents. To clear all calls, go to FaceTime > Settings > Remove All Recents. 

How to Schedule FaceTime Calls 

If you have an upcoming video conference planned, you can add a FaceTime call to your calendar: 

  1. Open the Calendar app and tap the plus icon to create a new event.  
  2. Enter the event title, tap Location or Video Call, and select FaceTime. 
  3. Specify the Date and Time to initiate the call.  
  4. Tap Invitees and enter the email addresses of the participants. 
  5. Finally, tap Add. 

At the scheduled time, click the Join button to start the call. 

You can also use third-party apps like Outlook to schedule calls with FaceTime links. 

Advanced FaceTime Tips

FaceTime features are super convenient. However, you can take FaceTime to the next level with these features: 

1. Remove Background Noise

During a FaceTime call, you can set the microphone to focus only on your voice, focus on others’ voices as well, or just behave normally.  

  • To isolate your voice during a call, open Control Center, select FaceTime Controls at the top, and tap Voice Isolation. On Mac, click the video icon on the menu bar and select Mic Mode. 
  • If you want to include sounds around you, select Wide Spectrum. It turns on the far field on your mic.  
  • You may choose Automatic to let your iPhone decide which mic mode to enable. 

2. Handoff Between Devices

Thanks to Apple’s Continuity features, you can easily switch FaceTime calls between devices seamlessly. Ensure your devices are signed in with the same Apple Account, have Bluetooth enabled, and are connected to the same Wi-Fi. 

Now, whenever you start a call on your iPhone and bring it near your Mac, you will see a notification to Move Call to This Mac. Click the notification to continue on your Mac.

Otherwise, click the gray video icon on the menu bar and select Switch. This works similarly across Apple devices if requirements are satisfied.

Tip: If you don’t want to receive calls on your other devices, go to Settings > Cellular > Calls on Other Devices and toggle off Allow Calls on Other Devices.

3. Use Live Captions 

If you are in a noisy place and can’t hear what others are saying, you can turn on Live Caption. It uses on-device intelligence to show real-time transcriptions on your display. 

On your iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > Apps > FaceTime and toggle on Live Captions. For Mac, access FaceTime > Settings and check the Live Captions box. Now, you will see a Live Captions box under the call controls. 

4. Announce FaceTime calls

You can set your iPhone to announce the caller’s name, making it easier to identify who is calling you. From the FaceTime settings, tap on Announce Calls and set it to announce the caller when connected to your car stereo, headphones, or both.

 

5. Record FaceTime Calls with Audio

Recording FaceTime calls can be useful for preserving memories, conducting interviews, or keeping records of important conversations. By default, you can’t record FaceTime video calls. So, we’ll be using the native Screen Recording feature.

During the call, open Control Center and select the Screen Recording icon to start recording. Then, tap and hold the control again and select Microphone to enable audio recording.

On Mac, press Command + Shift + 5 key together to access the screen recording toolbar. Select the entire screen recording icon, click Options, and select your Mac’s microphone. Finally, click Record.

FaceTime Privacy & Safety Tips

  1. Enable Sensitive Content Warning to avoid explicit video messages. 
  2. If you want to prevent spam calls, toggle on Silence Unknown Callers. You may also block persistent callers from FaceTime Settings > Blocked. 
  3. Test your camera and mic before important calls. 
  4. Save data on cellular by switching to Wi-Fi-only calls. Go to Settings > Cellular > Show All and toggle off FaceTime. 

  5. Ensure your correct email address is selected under “You Can Be Reached At.”
  6. To identify FaceTime calls, you can set a unique ringtone. From the FaceTime settings, select Notifications > Sounds and choose a tone.

Troubleshooting FaceTime Issues

Although FaceTime appears reliable, it can sometimes fail to work as expected. But worry not; you can easily fix it. Here are solutions to common FaceTime problems on iPhone, iPad, or Mac: 

FaceTime Won’t Activate: 

  • Check your internet connection and ensure you’re signed in with your Apple ID. 
  • Go to Settings > General > Date & Time and enable Set Automatically. 
  • Restart your device. 
  • Although rare, confirm there is no FaceTime outage from Apple’s end on the Apple System support page. 

Poor Video or Audio Quality: 

  • Switch to a stronger Wi-Fi network or move closer to your router. 
  • Check microphone/camera is working properly. 
  • Close background apps that might be using bandwidth. 
  • To solve the FaceTime issue on Mac, ensure the correct camera/mic is selected in the video icon on the menu bar > down arrow next to the camera. 

Can’t Join a Call: 

  • Verify the FaceTime link is valid and not expired. 
  • For non-Apple users, ensure they’re using Chrome or Edge browsers. 

Calls Keep Dropping: 

  • Update to the latest iOS/iPadOS/macOS version. 
  • Disable VPN or firewall temporarily to test connectivity. 

If problems continue, toggle off FaceTime from Settings, restart your device, and enable it again. As a last resort, visit the Apple Store or call Apple Support. 

Stay Connected with FaceTime!

FaceTime is more than just a video calling app—it’s your portal to stay connected, collaborate, and share moments with loved ones. From Live Reactions to screen sharing and scheduled calls, the possibilities are endless. Start exploring FaceTime now and make every call count.

FAQs

How to check FaceTime call duration?

Open the FaceTime app → Tap “i” beside a call → View call duration.

Can I FaceTime on my Apple Watch?

No, you can’t make video FaceTime calls on Apple Watch, but you can place or answer FaceTime audio calls using the Phone app or Siri when connected to your iPhone.

Can Android users join FaceTime?

Yes, via a shared FaceTime link in Chrome or Edge browser. They can’t start calls or use advanced features.

mainEntity.name: Can I hide photos in the Notes app instead?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Create a note, attach the photo, and lock the note using a password, Face ID, or Touch ID. The photo will no longer appear in the Photos app.

mainEntity.name: Is the Hidden Album encrypted?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. While it's protected by biometrics or passcode, it's not encrypted. Use third-party apps for added protection.

mainEntity.name: Do hidden photos sync across devices?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. They stay hidden on all devices if iCloud Photos is enabled. Use two-factor authentication to keep your account secure.

mainEntity.name: How to check FaceTime call duration?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open the FaceTime app → Tap “i” beside a call → View call duration.

mainEntity.name: Can I FaceTime on my Apple Watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can’t make video FaceTime calls on Apple Watch, but you can place or answer FaceTime audio calls using the Phone app or Siri when connected to your iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Can Android users join FaceTime?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, via a shared FaceTime link in Chrome or Edge browser. They can't start calls or use advanced features.

@graph.name: How to Set Up FaceTime On iPhone or iPad
@graph.description: Learn how to enable FaceTime on your iPhone or iPad in just a few steps so you can start video and audio calls with ease.

step.name: Open Settings
step.text: Unlock your iPhone or iPad and open the Settings app from your Home Screen.

itemListElement.text: Unlock your device and tap the Settings icon.

step.name: Navigate to FaceTime
step.text: Scroll down and tap on Apps, then select FaceTime from the list.

itemListElement.text: In the Settings menu, tap Apps and choose FaceTime.

step.name: Enable FaceTime
step.text: Turn on the FaceTime toggle to activate the service.

itemListElement.text: Tap the toggle to turn FaceTime ON.

step.name: Sign in with Apple ID
step.text: If prompted, sign in with your Apple ID to enable FaceTime services.

itemListElement.text: Enter your Apple ID credentials to sign in.

step.name: Choose Contact Options
step.text: Under 'You Can Be Reached By FaceTime At,' select the email or phone number you want to use.

itemListElement.text: Tap the email or number you prefer to use for FaceTime calls.

@graph.name: How to Set Up FaceTime On Mac
@graph.description: Easily activate and configure FaceTime on your Mac so you can make and receive video or audio calls effortlessly.

step.name: Open FaceTime App
step.text: Launch the FaceTime app from your Applications folder or search for it using Spotlight.

itemListElement.text: Open the FaceTime app from Applications or search for it using Spotlight.

step.name: Sign in with Apple ID
step.text: Use your Apple ID to sign in when prompted in the FaceTime app.

itemListElement.text: Enter your Apple ID email and password to sign in.

step.name: Open FaceTime Settings
step.text: Click FaceTime in the top menu bar and choose Settings to adjust your preferences.

itemListElement.text: Click on FaceTime in the menu bar and select Settings.

step.name: Choose Caller ID and Check Internet
step.text: Select your preferred email or phone number as the caller ID and ensure your Mac is connected to the internet.

itemListElement.text: Choose the email or number you want to use for FaceTime.
Verify your Mac has a stable internet connection.

blockGraphs.question: How to check FaceTime call duration?
blockGraphs.answer: Open the FaceTime app → Tap “i” beside a call → View call duration.

blockGraphs.question: Can I FaceTime on my Apple Watch?
blockGraphs.answer: No, you can’t make video FaceTime calls on Apple Watch, but you can place or answer FaceTime audio calls using the Phone app or Siri when connected to your iPhone.

blockGraphs.question: Can Android users join FaceTime?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes, via a shared FaceTime link in Chrome or Edge browser. They can't start calls or use advanced features.

keyPoints.title: Setting Up FaceTime on Apple Devices
keyPoints.explanation: You can set up FaceTime on iPhone, iPad, and Mac by signing in with your Apple ID, enabling FaceTime in settings, and choosing your contact reachability options.

keyPoints.title: Prerequisites for Using FaceTime
keyPoints.explanation: Ensure you have a compatible device, an Apple ID, a stable internet connection, and camera/microphone access; FaceTime must also be available in your region.

keyPoints.title: Making and Receiving Calls with FaceTime
keyPoints.explanation: Start a call by opening the app, selecting New FaceTime, and entering a contact, then choose video or audio; incoming calls can be answered, declined, or managed with options like holding.

keyPoints.title: Using Advanced FaceTime Features
keyPoints.explanation: Features like screen sharing, filters, Memoji, reactions, background blurring, and scheduling enhance your calls, making them more fun, interactive, and professional.

keyPoints.title: Troubleshooting Common FaceTime Issues
keyPoints.explanation: Fix problems like activation failure, poor quality, or dropping calls by checking your internet, updating software, verifying settings, or contacting Apple Support for persistent issues.

title.rendered: Snapchat Launches on Apple Watch—But There’s One Big Catch

content.rendered:
Snapchat, the go-to app for over 900 million users worldwide, has officially launched on the Apple Watch—though not with the full feature set fans might expect.

Since the Apple Watch lacks a built-in camera, you won’t be taking or sending Snaps just yet. Instead, the new app focuses on streamlined communication: preview incoming messages and respond using Scribble, voice dictation, emoji, or the on-screen keyboard (on supported models).

“Friends and family are some of the most important people in our lives, so keep the conversation going anytime, anywhere,” Snapchat said in an official statement.

A Step Into Multi-Device Expansion

Previously limited to smartphones and tablets, Snapchat’s arrival on the Apple Watch marks a significant expansion in its multi-device strategy. The company is clearly signaling that it wants to meet users where they are—whether that’s on mobile, tablet, desktop, or now, your wrist.

“Already we’re seeing our community enjoy using Snapchat across surfaces including tablet and web, in addition to mobile,” the company said. “This builds on our commitment to making Snapchat available across all the devices you use.”

The Apple Watch app gives Snapchat users a lightweight, quick-access way to stay connected on the go—perfect for glancing at messages while working out, commuting, or simply when your iPhone isn’t within reach.

No Snaps Yet—But Still a Useful Experience

Yes, Snapchat’s Apple Watch app doesn’t include camera-based features, meaning you can’t view or send Snaps. But its presence is still significant.

With many major platforms like Instagram, Slack, Amazon, Trello, and Uber having abandoned their Apple Watch apps, Snapchat’s entry feels both refreshing and forward-thinking.

It’s also a move that aligns well with the increasing popularity of wearable-first communication. The ability to check in with friends, send a quick emoji, or reply via voice right from your wrist gives Snapchat a subtle but powerful edge in the social media space.

Snapchat’s Focus on the Future of Wearables

Snapchat’s launch on Apple Watch shows it’s not just about flashy filters and viral lenses—it’s about convenience and connection.

While it’s not the full Snapchat experience, it reflects Snap Inc.’s growing interest in building across different platforms, including augmented reality wearables like Spectacles and now wrist-based devices like the Apple Watch.

So, would you use Snapchat on your Apple Watch to stay in touch without pulling out your phone? Let us know in the comments.

  • What Does the Green Dot Mean on Snapchat?
  • Snapchat Planets Order and Meaning – How Does It Work?

mainEntity.name: Can I hide photos in the Notes app instead?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Create a note, attach the photo, and lock the note using a password, Face ID, or Touch ID. The photo will no longer appear in the Photos app.

mainEntity.name: Is the Hidden Album encrypted?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. While it's protected by biometrics or passcode, it's not encrypted. Use third-party apps for added protection.

mainEntity.name: Do hidden photos sync across devices?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. They stay hidden on all devices if iCloud Photos is enabled. Use two-factor authentication to keep your account secure.

title.rendered: How to Add Favorites in Safari on iPhone, iPad, and Mac

content.rendered:
Tired of typing out the same website URLs every time? There’s a faster way. By adding sites to your Favorites in Safari, you can instantly access them from the Start Page or address bar—across your iPhone, iPad, and Mac. This guide shows you how to add, manage, and sync Safari Favorites seamlessly.

Table of Contents
  • What Are Favorites in Safari?
  • How to Add a Website to Favorites in Safari
    • On iPhone and iPad:
    • On Mac:
  • How to Access Favorites in Safari
    • On iPhone and iPad:
    • On Mac:
  • How to Edit or Remove Favorites
    • On iPhone and iPad:
    • On Mac:
  • How to Change the Favorites Folder in Safari
    • On iPhone and iPad
    • On Mac
  • How to Sync Favorites Across Devices with iCloud
    • On iPhone and iPad:
    • On Mac:
  • One Tap Closer to the Web…

What Are Favorites in Safari?

Favorites are a special kind of bookmark in Safari. They appear at the top of the Start Page and in address bar suggestions for quicker access. Plus, with iCloud sync enabled, your favorites stay updated across all your Apple devices automatically.

How to Add a Website to Favorites in Safari

Adding your frequently visited websites to your favorites in Safari empowers you to access them with just a tap or click, eliminating the need to enter the URL every time you want to visit them.

On iPhone and iPad:

  1. Open Safari and visit the site you want to favorite.
  2. Tap the Share button at the bottom center. 
  3. Select the Add to Favorites option in the Share Sheet. 
  4. Rename the site if you like → Tap Save.

On Mac:

  1. Launch Safari and go to the desired website.
  2. Press Command (⌘) + D. 
  3. In the popup, choose Favorites as the save location.
  4. Give the website a unique name if you want to, then click the Add button.

How to Access Favorites in Safari

Whether you’re using an iPhone, iPad, or Mac, there are multiple ways you can access your favorite websites in Safari.

On iPhone and iPad:

  • Start Page: Open a new tab. Favorites appear at the top.
  • Address bar: Tap the address bar at the bottom, and your favorite websites will instantly appear at the top for quicker access.
  • Bookmarks: Tap the Bookmarks icon → Tap Favorites to view your favorite websites.

On Mac:

  • Start Page: Click the + button at the top right corner to open a new tab, and your Favorites will appear at the top of the Start Page.
  • Smart Search Field: Click the address bar at the top, and your Favorites will show up under it.
  • Bookmarks Sidebar: Press Command (⌘) + Control + 1 to open.

How to Edit or Remove Favorites

There comes a time when you no longer visit a website as frequently as you used to; thus, removing such websites from your favorites list makes more sense. Here’s how:

On iPhone and iPad:

  1. Open Safari and create a new tab.
  2. Long press the website icon you want to edit or remove under Favorites on the Start Page.

  3. Choose Edit to rename or Delete to remove.

Alternative: Go to Bookmarks tab → Long-press the site name → Tap Delete.

On Mac:

  1. Open a new Safari Start Page.
  2. Control-click the website icon under Favorites.
  3. Select Rename or Delete.

If the Favorites section is hidden on Start Page:

  1. Click the Sidebar button in the toolbar. 
  2. Click the Bookmark option in the sidebar. 
  3. Control-click the website you want to remove under the Favorites section. 
  4. Choose the Delete option in the pop-up menu.

How to Change the Favorites Folder in Safari

Want to separate work and personal sites? You can customize which bookmark folder Safari uses for Favorites.

On iPhone and iPad

Create a Folder:

  1. Tap the Bookmark icon at the bottom > Tap Edit.
  2. Tap New Folder in the bottom left corner.

  3. Enter the folder’s name and tap done.

Set as Favorites:

  1. Open Settings → Apps → Safari.
  2. Locate and tap Favorites under the General section.

  3. Select the desired shortcuts folder.

Now, instead of the websites in the Favorites folder, the website you added to the newly created bookmarks folder will appear on the Safari Start Page.

On Mac

Create a Folder:

  1. Click the Sidebar icon at the top left.

  2. Here, Control-click on Favorites, then select New Folder in the contextual menu.

  3. Give your new folder a name and hit Return.

Set as Favorites:

  1. Click Safari in the top menu bar and select Settings from the drop-down menu.

  2. Under the General tab, click the dropdown next to Favorites.
  3. Select the new folder you just created.

How to Sync Favorites Across Devices with iCloud

To ensure seamless access to your Favorites across iPhone, iPad, and Mac:

On iPhone and iPad:

  1. Open Settings → Tap Apple ID → iCloud.
  2. Tap Show All under Apps Using iCloud.
  3. Make sure Safari is toggled on.

On Mac:

  1. Go to System Settings → Click iCloud in the sidebar.
  2. Click the See All button next to Saved to iCloud.

  3. Locate and toggle on Safari if it’s not already enabled.

One Tap Closer to the Web…

Adding websites to Favorites in Safari saves time and keeps your most-used sites just a tap away. Whether you’re organizing work tools or your go-to news sources, Safari’s Favorites feature—combined with iCloud syncing—makes browsing more personal and efficient.

Take a few minutes today to customize your Favorites folder, and supercharge your Safari experience.

FAQs

How do I transfer my favorites from iPhone to iPad?

Ensure both devices are signed in with the same Apple ID and have Safari iCloud sync enabled.

Why are my favorites missing from Safari on iPad?

They may be hidden due to iCloud sync being disabled, using a different Apple ID, or internet connectivity issues.

Check out these helpful guides too:

  • How to change the default search engine in Safari
  • How to delete Reading List in Safari
  • How to Use Safari Extensions on iPhone, iPad, and Mac

mainEntity.name: Can I hide photos in the Notes app instead?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Create a note, attach the photo, and lock the note using a password, Face ID, or Touch ID. The photo will no longer appear in the Photos app.

mainEntity.name: Is the Hidden Album encrypted?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. While it's protected by biometrics or passcode, it's not encrypted. Use third-party apps for added protection.

mainEntity.name: Do hidden photos sync across devices?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. They stay hidden on all devices if iCloud Photos is enabled. Use two-factor authentication to keep your account secure.

mainEntity.name: How to check FaceTime call duration?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open the FaceTime app → Tap “i” beside a call → View call duration.

mainEntity.name: Can I FaceTime on my Apple Watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can’t make video FaceTime calls on Apple Watch, but you can place or answer FaceTime audio calls using the Phone app or Siri when connected to your iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Can Android users join FaceTime?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, via a shared FaceTime link in Chrome or Edge browser. They can't start calls or use advanced features.

mainEntity.name: How do I transfer my favorites from iPhone to iPad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ensure both devices are signed in with the same Apple ID and have Safari iCloud sync enabled.

mainEntity.name: Why are my favorites missing from Safari on iPad?

acceptedAnswer.text: They may be hidden due to iCloud sync being disabled, using a different Apple ID, or internet connectivity issues.

title.rendered: How to Scan QR Code on iPhone: Easy Methods Explained

content.rendered:
Imagine never having to type out long website addresses or search for contact details again thanks to Quick Response (QR) codes, it’s as simple as that! With just a quick scan using your iPhone or iPad, you can visit a webpage, call a number, add contacts, or even join a Wi-Fi network in seconds. QR codes are designed to make your daily life easier and more efficient, allowing you to access information or take action instantly.

In this guide, I’ll walk you through everything you need to know about scanning QR codes,
fixing common problems, staying safe, and making the most of this handy technology. Whether you’re shopping, networking, or getting event details, you’ll find tips to help you use QR codes with confidence and ease.

Table of Contents

  1. How to scan a QR code with the Camera app
  2. How to use Code Scanner from Control Center
  3. How to scan QR codes with the Wallet app
  4. How to scan QR codes with Chrome or third-party apps
  5. How to scan QR codes from images using Live Text
  6. Troubleshooting QR code scanning issues
  7. Security and safety tips
  8. Accessibility options
  9. Advanced and creative uses for QR codes
  10. How to create QR codes quickly

1. How to Scan a QR Code with the Camera App

  1. Open the Camera app.
  2. Select the rear-facing camera.
  3. Point your camera at the QR code on a screen, paper, or product. Hold steady for a few seconds.

  4. Tap the notification that appears at the top of your screen to open the link or action.
Note: If you don’t see a notification, open Settings → Camera and ensure “Scan QR Codes” is turned on.

2. How to Use Code Scanner from Control Center

  1. Open Settings and tap Control Center.
  2. Scroll down and tap the green + icon for “Code Scanner” to add it.
  3. Access Control Center (swipe down from the top right on Face ID iPhones or up from the bottom on Home button models).
  4. Tap the Code Scanner icon and point it at a QR code. The scanner will open the link automatically.

Tip: Code Scanner includes a flashlight option for scanning in low light.

3. How to Scan QR Codes with the Wallet App

The Wallet app scans QR codes for boarding passes, event tickets, and coupons, letting you store and easily access digital versions for travel, entertainment, and shopping.

  1. Tap the + icon at the top of the “Passes” section.
  2. Tap “Scan Code to Add a Pass.”
  3. If you don’t see the + icon, scroll down your passes, tap “Edit Passes,” then tap “Scan Code” at the bottom.

4. How to Scan QR Codes with Chrome or Third-Party Apps

Many apps now include QR scanning as a standard feature, enabling users to quickly scan QR codes without needing separate tools. In addition to basic scanning, some apps provide advanced options such as saving scanned information, generating custom QR codes, and integrating with other app functions for a more seamless experience.

Third-party apps, such as QR Code Reader & QR Scanner, QR Code & Barcode Scanner, or QR Code Reader – QR Scan, further enhance functionality by allowing users to keep a history of scans and create personalized QR codes, making it easier to manage and utilize QR technology in various contexts.

  1. From the iPhone Home Screen or App Library,long-press the Chrome app.
  2. Tap Scan QR Code.

  3. Permit the app to access the device camera and point it to a QR code.

5. How to Scan QR Codes from Images Using Live Text

If you receive a QR code in a photo, screenshot, or see one on a website, you can use Live Text to scan it:

  1. Open the Photos app and select the image with the QR code.
  2. Look for the Live Text icon in the corner.
  3. Tap the icon, then tap the QR code itself. You’ll see options to open the link, copy, or share it.

Safari Tip: If you spot a QR code on a website, tap and hold it, then select “Open QR Code” from the menu.

6. Troubleshooting QR Code Scanning Issues

Have trouble scanning a QR code? Try these solutions:

  1. Focus issues: Tap the screen where the QR code is to help the camera focus. Try moving your device a bit closer or farther for a clearer picture.
  2. Lighting conditions: Make sure the area is bright enough. You can use your iPhone’s flashlight, but try not to shine it directly on the code to avoid glare.
  3. Damaged or unclear codes: Look for scratches, smudges, or faded spots on the QR code. If the code is damaged, it might not scan.
  4. No notification appears: Check that “Scan QR Codes” is turned on in Settings → Camera.
  5. App permissions: Make sure the scanning app can use the camera in Settings.

7. Security and Safety Tips

Stay safe when scanning QR codes:

  1. Scan codes only from sources you trust. Avoid scanning codes from strange emails, random flyers, or websites you don’t know.
  2. Look at the link before opening it. The Camera app shows the web address—check it before you tap.
  3. Keep your iPhone and apps up to date to stay safe from security risks.

8. Accessibility Options

For users with visual impairments, scanning QR codes can be easier with these tools:

  1. Code Scanner in the Control Center provides audio feedback and works well with VoiceOver.
  2. VoiceOver can announce when a QR code is detected and help you open the link without needing to see the screen.

9. Advanced and Creative Uses for QR Codes

QR codes aren’t just for web links! Unlock new possibilities with these advanced uses and pro tips. In fact, QR codes offer advantages over RFID, including lower costs, more straightforward implementation, and greater accessibility.

  1. Share Wi-Fi access: Make a QR code with your Wi-Fi details so guests can connect right away—no need to type a password. Print it for your home or office, or save it to your Photos for quick sharing.
  2. Digital business cards: Share your contact info, website, or social media with one scan. You can add your logo or brand colors to give a more professional look.
  3. Event invitations: Link to RSVPs, schedules, or maps for weddings, conferences, or parties. Place QR codes on printed or digital invitations so guests can easily access the information they need.
  4. Automate QR code sharing with Shortcuts: Use the Shortcuts app to quickly make and send QR codes for your contact info, Wi-Fi, or events. This saves time and makes sharing easier.
  5. Save and reuse QR codes: Keep your most-used QR codes in your Photos app, add them to Wallet for quick access, or share them with AirDrop, Messages, or email.
  6. Accessibility for advanced uses: Add text labels or audio instructions to QR codes so everyone, including people with disabilities, can use them.
Etiquette Tip: When sharing QR codes in public or professional settings, label them clearly (e.g., “Scan to Connect to Wi-Fi”) and always provide an alternative way to access the information if possible.

10. How to Create QR Codes Quickly

Do you want to share a link, contact, or Wi-Fi password? Here’s how to create a QR code directly from your iPhone or iPad:

  1. Visit the-qrcode-generator.com or another reputable QR code generator in your browser.
  2. Choose the type of code (URL, contact, Wi-Fi, event, etc.).
  3. Enter your details and download or display the QR code for others to scan.
  4. Save the QR code image to your Photos app for easy access and sharing.
Pro Tips:
  • In Chrome, right-click a page and select “Create QR code for this page” to generate one instantly.
  • Use QR code generators that allow branding (like adding a logo or colors) for a polished, professional look.
  • For automation, use the Shortcuts app to set up a workflow that creates and shares QR codes for your most frequently used information.

What You Should Take Away

With these tips and advanced methods, scanning and sharing QR codes on your iPhone or iPad becomes a breeze—no matter if you’re welcoming friends to your home Wi-Fi, networking with colleagues, promoting your business, or planning an event. QR codes are also a handy way to share contact info, open websites, or even make payments. If you’d like some creative suggestions or need help with a particular situation, just let me know in the comments—I’m here to help!

FAQs

Can you scan a QR code without an app?

Yes! The built-in Camera app or Code Scanner in the Control Center works without the need for third-party apps.

Which iPhones can scan QR codes?

All iPhones running iOS 11 or later can scan QR codes using built-in features.

Why won’t my iPhone scan a QR code?

No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings.

mainEntity.name: Can I hide photos in the Notes app instead?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Create a note, attach the photo, and lock the note using a password, Face ID, or Touch ID. The photo will no longer appear in the Photos app.

mainEntity.name: Is the Hidden Album encrypted?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. While it's protected by biometrics or passcode, it's not encrypted. Use third-party apps for added protection.

mainEntity.name: Do hidden photos sync across devices?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. They stay hidden on all devices if iCloud Photos is enabled. Use two-factor authentication to keep your account secure.

mainEntity.name: How to check FaceTime call duration?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open the FaceTime app → Tap “i” beside a call → View call duration.

mainEntity.name: Can I FaceTime on my Apple Watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can’t make video FaceTime calls on Apple Watch, but you can place or answer FaceTime audio calls using the Phone app or Siri when connected to your iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Can Android users join FaceTime?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, via a shared FaceTime link in Chrome or Edge browser. They can't start calls or use advanced features.

mainEntity.name: How do I transfer my favorites from iPhone to iPad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ensure both devices are signed in with the same Apple ID and have Safari iCloud sync enabled.

mainEntity.name: Why are my favorites missing from Safari on iPad?

acceptedAnswer.text: They may be hidden due to iCloud sync being disabled, using a different Apple ID, or internet connectivity issues.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! The built-in Camera app or Code Scanner in the Control Center works without the need for third-party apps.

acceptedAnswer.text: All iPhones running iOS 11 or later can scan QR codes using built-in features.

title.rendered: New ChatGPT for Mac Update Adds Game-Changing Record Mode and Cloud Drive Access

content.rendered:
OpenAI is stepping up its mission to transform ChatGPT for Mac into an all-in-one productivity assistant. The company has introduced two powerful new features—Record Mode and Cloud Drive Integration—for users on ChatGPT Team, Enterprise, and Edu plans. These updates aim to simplify how teams capture, retrieve, and act on information—right from within ChatGPT—cutting out the need to toggle between multiple apps or platforms.

ChatGPT Record Mode: From Voice to Smart Notes Instantly

Mac users will now spot a Record button alongside their prompt tools. A quick click launches a floating widget that instantly begins recording and transcribing audio in real time.

But it doesn’t stop at transcription.

ChatGPT automatically transforms spoken content into structured notes, including:

  • Summaries
  • Key points
  • Action items
  • Open questions

This isn’t like Zoom or Notion, where bots need to be invited to meetings. Instead, ChatGPT records locally on your Mac, listening to your device’s audio—no invites, no bots, no distractions. It’s built for effortless, secure note-taking on the fly.

Watch ChatGPT Record Mode in Action

Cloud Drive Integration: Smarter Answers with Your Own Data

Another powerful addition is Cloud Drive Integration. ChatGPT now connects directly with your:

  • Google Drive
  • Dropbox
  • OneDrive
  • Box
  • SharePoint

You can now ask natural language queries like:

  • “What were our Q1 OKRs last year?”
  • “How many shipments used sea freight in our latest logistics report?”

ChatGPT searches your connected files in real time and returns structured, source-linked answers—without compromising file privacy or data security. All permissions and access controls are respected, and OpenAI confirms no documents are used for training the model.

Expanded Connectors for More Contextual Power

Along with cloud drives, OpenAI added integrations for top productivity tools, including:

  • HubSpot
  • Linear
  • GitHub
  • Gmail
  • Google Calendar
  • Google Docs, Sheets, Slides
  • Outlook
  • Microsoft Teams

These connectors power Canvas, OpenAI’s visual workspace, enabling users to build reports, summaries, and presentations using both internal data and external insights.

The update also brings support for Anthropic’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) in ChatGPT’s Deep Research mode. As more services—like Replit, Atlassian, Zapier, and Cloudflare—embrace MCP, ChatGPT’s ecosystem becomes a more dynamic AI hub for teams and developers.

The Future of Work Is AI-Augmented

From recording and summarizing meetings to querying your entire cloud drive, these tools underscore a big shift: ChatGPT is evolving from a chatbot into a full-stack productivity platform.

Whether you’re in sales, product, support, or leadership—this could redefine how teams collaborate, document, and move fast.

Will you try Record Mode or connect your drive? Share your thoughts below!

  • Meta Launches AI App That Knows You Better Than ChatGPT
  • How to run an LLM locally on your Mac
  • I tried DeepSeek on my iPhone: Here’s how it compares to ChatGPT

title.rendered: Best Music Games for iPhone and iPad

content.rendered:
The fusion of superb music and scintillating games is too lethal to be ignored! That’s why most of us like to be entertained while having a blast at our favorite games. Having tried out numerous musical adventures, I have decided to create an elite list of the best music games for iPhone and iPad, which I’m sure you’d like to have a sneak peek at. To ensure your different tastes have the right match, I have picked out a variety of different games. Apart from being very interesting, they are relatively easy to play. Once you get started with them, you will feel like going on and on. Ready to have a go at my top 10 music games for iOS? Let’s dive right in!

1. SongPop Classic – Music Trivia

If you think you know everything about music, then this is the game you should try your hands on. SongPop 2 has more than 100K real music clips, and your job is to identify the artist and title as fast as you can. Also, you can challenge your friends or other music lovers worldwide. Lastly, the game also offers a daily multiplayer tournament, so make sure you are ready for the challenge.

Price: Free
Download

2. Piano Tiles 2

This one is an absolute gem courtesy of the fabulous rhythm and impressive UI. It’s pretty simple to play. All you have to do is tap the black tiles according to the melody; making sure you don’t miss out on anyone.

The game consists of different types of songs like classic, bang, and original, which keep you thrilled throughout. With the top-notch sound, the songs never let any boredom creep up. There is a challenge mode that puts your skill to the real test. Face more challenges and get a lot of bonuses to be the ultimate player!

Price: Free
Download

3. Real Drum

Do you love playing the drum? If yes, you would really enjoy having a go at this drum simulator app. To play this game, simply tap your fingers on the pads of the drum.

It features 60 examples of rhythms and 24 backing track songs. You can also record the game to keep a tab on the progress. Boasting studio sound quality, it has the charisma to delight you to the core.

Price: Free
Download

4. Dancing Line

This fun music game is a fast-paced challenge in which you have to move through obstacles and traps while also playing the music. It features different worlds of increasing difficulty, which each paints a unique picture.

Guide an ever-growing Line through a variety of environments, listening carefully to the music. Tap the screen to make sharp turns, dodging obstacles, and reacting as the scene changes before your eyes.

Price: Free ($5.99 to remove ads)
Download

5. My Singing Monsters: Dawn of Fire

My Singing Monsters is one gem of a game with a completely innovative concept. You’ll need to travel back in time when monsters first erupted. Every monster has a unique voice, so make sure you keep unlocking new characters. Also, you can breed your monsters to develop a unique one with a new voice. Assemble them to make your own orchestra. There’s another bunch of features in this game, so just click the download link, as the game is entirely free.

Price: Free

Download

6. Steve Reich’s Clapping Music

No musical instruments? No problem, as long as you can clap. The clapping game will help you improve your rhythm, as it includes music using only claps. The game offers three different difficulty levels, so make sure you start from easy and then advance to the pro level. The concept is pretty fresh and worth a try. And yes, do enter the competitions and you could have a chance to perform live.

Price: Free
Download

7. Groove Planet

Our planet Earth has already been acquainted with music; it’s time to expand the horizon to other planets. That’s the theme of the Groove Planet game. You are the mayor and everything to be built is by using the music notes. The game has stunning graphics, and it also supports challenging other players. So in short, you aren’t completely alone in the race, people around the world are your serious competition. Groove Planet is free to play but with optional in-app purchases.

Price: Free
Download

8. 123 Kids Fun MUSIC

If you are in quest of a fantastic music game for your preschool kid, you should give a game a serious look at this game. It’s designed to encourage kids to create music and explore the world of music. The app has 25 instruments, such as xylophone, drums, guitars, flutes, saxophone, etc., to explore.

This game features several activities that can enhance kids’ motor skills and creativity. Colorful graphics and vibrant sounds bring a lot of fun into the play.

Price: Free
Download

Your pick?

Which one of these fantastic music games have you chosen for your playtime? It would be nice to know its name and the type of games you enjoy playing a lot.

You might want to have a look at these posts as well:

  • Guitar Apps for iPhone and iPad
